scope: Editorial first-orientation suggestions for the 64 parks retained in this planner, not measured size or popularity rankings.
coordinateSource: NPS official structured facility records. Approximate facility pins, not verified parking entrances or navigable vehicle approaches.

acad.reason: Orientation for Mount Desert Island and the main park-loop area.
acad.note: Seasonal facility; Schoodic and Isle au Haut need separate approaches.

alternatives.name: Schoodic Institute Welcome Center at Rockefeller Hall

arch.reason: Orientation just inside the park entrance.
arch.note: Park entry rules and parking availability need a travel-year check.

badl.reason: Orientation for the North Unit and Badlands Loop Road.
badl.note: White River serves the separate South Unit.

bibe.reason: Central orientation hub for the park road network.
bibe.note: Other districts are far apart; do not treat one center as the whole visit.

bisc.note: The mainland center is not an island landing; most marine outings need separate boat arrangements.

blca.reason: Orientation for the South Rim overlooks.
blca.note: The North Rim is a separate road approach; there is no road bridge across the canyon.

brca.reason: Orientation near the park entrance and main amphitheater road.
brca.note: Check shuttle service, snow and parking conditions.

primary.name: Island in the Sky Visitor Center

cany.reason: Starting point for the mesa-top scenic-drive district.
cany.note: The Needles and Maze have separate entrances; no internal road connects the districts.

primary.name: Capitol Reef National Park Visitor Center

care.reason: Orientation for Fruita and the central scenic-drive area.
care.note: Remote districts require separate road and vehicle research.

cave.reason: Starting point for cave information and tours.
cave.note: The pin is at the surface facility; cave admission, tickets and underground access are separate.

chir.reason: Orientation on the main Bonita Canyon approach.
chir.note: Mountain-road and vehicle restrictions still need checking.

primary.name: Channel Islands National Park Visitor Center

chis.note: This center is on the mainland, not on an island or a guaranteed boat departure point. Island transport is separate.

alternatives.name: Scorpion Ranch Visitor Center on Santa Cruz Island

cong.reason: Orientation at the main boardwalk area.
cong.note: Flooding and trail conditions can change access.

crla.note: Rim Visitor Center is a seasonal alternative; snow can limit the approach.

cuva.reason: Central starting point for park information.
cuva.note: The park follows a long corridor; other trailheads need their own directions.

dena.reason: Orientation in the road-accessible entrance area.
dena.note: Seasonal center; Murie Science and Learning Center is an entrance-area alternative. Park-road access is separate.

deva.reason: Central orientation hub for the Furnace Creek area.
deva.note: Heat, flood damage and road conditions need a current check.

drto.note: Boat or seaplane access only; there is no driving route to this pin. Book transport separately.

ever.reason: Orientation for the Homestead entrance and main park road.
ever.note: Shark Valley and Gulf Coast are separate approaches; this pin does not represent all districts.

gaar.reason: Road-accessible orientation in Coldfoot for the Brooks Range.
gaar.note: Outside the park. There is no road into Gates of the Arctic; flight or wilderness access must be arranged separately.

alternatives.name: Bettles Ranger Station and Visitor Center

glac.reason: Orientation near the west entrance and Lake McDonald area.
glac.note: St. Mary serves the east side; Going-to-the-Sun Road is seasonal.

primary.name: Glacier Bay National Park Visitor Center

glba.reason: Orientation at Bartlett Cove near Gustavus.
glba.note: Reach Gustavus by air or water first; visiting the bay requires separate boat arrangements. Seasonal facility.

grba.reason: Orientation at the cave-tour and Wheeler Peak approach.
grba.note: Great Basin Visitor Center in Baker is another useful arrival stop. Cave tickets and mountain-road access are separate.

grca.reason: Orientation at the main South Rim visitor plaza.
grca.note: Use designated parking and walk or shuttle to facilities. Other rims require separate approaches.

grsa.reason: Orientation near the main park entrance.
grsa.note: Sand, creek, weather and Medano Pass vehicle conditions require separate review.

grsm.reason: Starting point for the Gatlinburg and Tennessee approach.
grsm.note: Oconaluftee is the corresponding North Carolina arrival stop.

grte.reason: Orientation near Moose and the southern park approach.
grte.note: Colter Bay serves the northern lakes area. Facility seasons vary.

gumo.reason: Orientation at the main US 62/180 entrance.
gumo.note: Dog Canyon has a separate approach; there is no through-road across the park.

hale.reason: Orientation near the summit's principal viewing area.
hale.note: Summit access and sunrise reservations require review. Kīpahulu is a separate coastal district with no through-road.

havo.reason: Current NPS-listed visitor-information location near Kīlauea Military Camp.
havo.note: Reviewed November 2026: use this Welcome Center rather than assuming the older Kīlauea Visitor Center is operating. Recheck construction changes.

primary.name: Fordyce Bathhouse Visitor Center and Museum

hosp.note: The building is on a pedestrian-oriented historic street; use legal parking and walk to the center.

primary.name: Dorothy Buell Memorial Visitor Center (Indiana Dunes Visitor Center)

indu.reason: Orientation at the shared Indiana Dunes visitor-information center.
indu.note: Beach parking and individual lakefront sites are separate destinations.

isro.reason: Orientation for a Rock Harbor island arrival.
isro.note: Boat or seaplane only. Windigo serves the island's other end; Houghton is a mainland planning center, not the island.

jeff.reason: Orientation at the Arch visitor complex.
jeff.note: Use designated downtown parking and walk to the entrance; the pin is not a vehicle drop-off or garage. Security screening applies.

jotr.reason: Orientation in Joshua Tree town before the west entrance.
jotr.note: Outside the entrance. The similarly named National Park Visitor Center in Twentynine Palms serves another approach.

alternatives.name: Joshua Tree National Park Visitor Center

katm.reason: Orientation for the park's Brooks Camp bear-viewing area.
katm.note: Floatplane or boat access; no road reaches Brooks Camp. King Salmon is a separate gateway center. Bear-safety orientation and transport are required.

primary.name: Kenai Fjords National Park Visitor Center

kefj.note: The center is seasonal; Exit Glacier has a separate road approach, and fjord outings need boat arrangements.

kica.reason: Orientation in Grant Grove Village for the main western approach.
kica.note: Cedar Grove is farther into the canyon on a seasonal road.

kova.note: Outside the park. There is no road to Kobuk Valley; a visit here does not replace an arranged park flight.

lacl.reason: Orientation at the Port Alsworth gateway.
lacl.note: Arrive by small aircraft or other arranged remote transport; there is no road from Anchorage. Other park areas may use different landings.

lavo.note: The park highway is seasonal; Loomis Museum serves the northwest approach.

maca.reason: Main cave-tour and park-information starting point.
maca.note: Reserve the specific cave tour separately; the pin is not an underground route.

primary.name: Mesa Verde Visitor and Research Center

meve.reason: Orientation near the park entrance before the long mesa-top drive.
meve.note: Cliff-dwelling tour locations and tickets are separate; allow additional driving from this center.

primary.name: Henry M Jackson Memorial Visitor Center

mora.reason: Orientation at Paradise, a principal mountain-viewing and hiking area.
mora.note: Paradise road access and facility hours vary with snow. Sunrise has a separate seasonal approach.

neri.reason: Orientation near the New River Gorge Bridge.
neri.note: Sandstone and the southern gorge have separate approaches.

noca.reason: Orientation near Newhalem on the SR 20 corridor.
noca.note: Stehekin's Golden West center requires a separate boat, air or trail approach; seasonal road and facility access vary.

npsa.reason: Orientation in the Pago Pago area on Tutuila.
npsa.note: The center is outside the main park units; outer-island trips require separate transport.

olym.note: Rainforest and coast districts are far apart; Hoh is a separate destination, not a nearby branch.

pefo.reason: Orientation at the northern I-40 approach.
pefo.note: Rainbow Forest Museum serves the southern US 180 entrance.

pinn.reason: Visitor-information starting point by the east-side campground.
pinn.note: NPS lists this as a park store at the east visitor-center area. East and west entrances have no connecting road; ranger staffing varies.

redw.reason: Orientation near Orick for the southern redwood and coastal areas.
redw.note: Hiouchi serves the far northern parks; this is a spread-out park complex.

romo.reason: Orientation near Estes Park and the east-side entrance.
romo.note: Kawuneeche serves Grand Lake; Trail Ridge Road is a seasonal connection.

sagu.reason: Orientation for the Tucson Mountain and western saguaro district.
sagu.note: Rincon Mountain is a separate district across Tucson; there is no internal park road between them.

sequ.reason: Orientation just inside the Ash Mountain entrance before the mountain drive.
sequ.note: Giant Forest Museum serves the sequoia-grove area farther uphill. Vehicle-length and winter-road restrictions matter.

primary.name: Harry F. Byrd Sr. Visitor Center

shen.reason: Orientation at Big Meadows in the central Skyline Drive area.
shen.note: Dickey Ridge is the useful northern arrival alternative; both facilities and Skyline Drive have seasonal limitations.

thro.reason: Orientation in Medora for the South Unit.
thro.note: The North Unit is a separate road trip; the units have different time zones.

viis.reason: Orientation near the passenger-ferry arrival on St. John.
viis.note: Reach St. John by ferry or other arranged boat transport; the center is not a mainland driving destination.

voya.reason: Orientation at a road-accessible mainland visitor hub.
voya.note: Most park exploration is on water; Kabetogama and Ash River serve other lake approaches.

whsa.reason: Orientation at the main entrance before Dunes Drive.
whsa.note: Check current road and temporary closure notices.

wica.reason: Main cave-tour and park-orientation starting point.
wica.note: Check cave-tour availability and ticket rules separately.

primary.name: Wrangell-St. Elias Visitor Center in Copper Center

wrst.reason: Road-accessible orientation for this very large park.
wrst.note: This is not Kennecott. McCarthy/Kennecott need a separate long approach and local access planning.

yell.reason: Orientation for the signature geyser basin and popular Old Faithful area.
yell.note: This is an interior destination, not the nearest entrance. Road seasons matter; Canyon and Mammoth are useful alternatives.

yose.reason: Current visitor-information starting point near Yosemite Village parking.
yose.note: Use designated parking and walk to the center. This is the newer Welcome Center, not the former Valley Visitor Center.

zion.reason: Orientation at the south entrance and main canyon shuttle hub.
zion.note: Use designated parking; canyon shuttle rules and parking demand vary. Kolob Canyons has a separate entrance.
